title: How to reset a forgotten Windows password
problem: You cannot sign in because you forgot your password or it has expired.
steps: On the sign-in screen, check that Caps Lock is off and the keyboard language is English.
If your password has expired, sign-in will ask you to create a new one. Choose at least 12 characters.
If you forgot it, call the Service Desk or send a ticket from your phone. We will confirm your identity with your employee ID.
The technician sets a temporary password. Sign in with it and Windows will ask you to choose a new one.
Sign out and sign in again with the new password. Update the password on your phone mail app too (see KB-05).
still: If the account says 'locked', read KB-02. If it says 'account disabled', contact your manager.
prevent: Use a long phrase you can remember. Never write the password on a sticky note. Do not reuse it for other websites.
ticket: Accounts and Access, Medium (High if the shift starts within one hour)
shot: The Windows sign-in screen with the 'Reset' message; the 'Change a password' screen.

title: Your account is locked after wrong passwords
applies: Windows accounts, phones with company mail
problem: You see 'The referenced account is currently locked out'.
steps: Wait 15 minutes; the account unlocks by itself.
Think about where an old password is still saved: your phone mail app, Wi-Fi settings, mapped drives, a second laptop.
Update the password in those places, or remove the old account from the phone.
If you cannot wait, ask the Service Desk to unlock the account. We will also tell you which device caused the lockout.
still: If the account locks again within an hour, a device is still using the old password. Open a ticket and give us the device names.
prevent: After every password change, update the phone mail app first.
shot: The lockout message; phone 'Accounts' settings screen.

title: How to connect to the company VPN
problem: You need to reach company files or applications from outside the office.
steps: Check that your home internet works: open any website.
Open the VPN app from the Start menu and choose the profile 'EV-Fleet-VPN'.
Enter your company username and password, then approve the MFA prompt on your phone.
Wait for the status 'Connected', then open the shared folder or application.
When finished, press Disconnect.
still: If it says 'connection timed out': try a mobile hotspot. If the hotspot works, your home router blocks the VPN; ask us to switch your profile to TCP 443 (see KB-04).
prevent: Keep the VPN app updated. Do not use free VPN apps on company laptops.
ticket: Network and VPN, High if you cannot work; Medium otherwise

title: VPN says 'connection timed out' (for support staff)
problem: The user has internet but the VPN client cannot connect.
steps: Test the internet: 'ping 8.8.8.8' in a terminal.
Test DNS: 'ping google.com'. If only this fails, see KB-15.
Ask the user to connect through a mobile hotspot. If the VPN connects, the user's network blocks the VPN port.
Change the user's profile to use TCP 443, which is rarely blocked.
Check the VPN gateway log for the user's name and confirm the session appears.
still: If the hotspot also fails, check the gateway status and the user's account (locked or MFA problem).
prevent: Document the port and protocol in the VPN profile template.
ticket: Network and VPN (assigned to Infrastructure and Network L2)
shot: The VPN profile setting that selects TCP 443.

title: Setting up company mail on your computer and phone
applies: Outlook on Windows 11; iPhone and Android
problem: You are new, or you got a new phone, and need company mail.
steps: On the computer: open Outlook, choose Add account, type your company e-mail address, then enter your password and MFA code.
On the phone: open Settings, Mail (or Accounts), Add account, choose Microsoft 365 or Exchange, and sign in.
If the phone says it cannot verify the server identity, check that the date and time are set to automatic.
Send yourself a test e-mail and check it arrives on both devices.
Do not install other mail apps that ask for your password.
still: If Outlook keeps asking for a password, open Control Panel, Credential Manager, Windows Credentials, remove the old Office entries, and restart Outlook.
prevent: Keep the phone's date and time on automatic.
shot: Outlook 'Add account' window; phone Accounts screen.

title: Your laptop is slow: five quick checks
problem: The laptop takes minutes to start or freezes while working.
steps: Restart the laptop. A laptop that has not been restarted for weeks gets slow.
Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager. Look at the CPU, Memory and Disk columns. If one is near 100%, note which app uses it.
Open the 'Startup apps' tab and disable apps you do not need at start (not antivirus or VPN).
Open Settings, Windows Update and install pending updates. Restart.
Open Settings, System, Storage, Temporary files and remove temporary files. Keep at least 15% of the disk free.
still: If the disk is always at 100% or the battery drains fast, open a ticket. We will check the disk health and battery report.
prevent: Restart weekly. Close browser tabs you are not using.
shot: Task Manager showing the Startup apps tab; Storage settings page.

title: Wi-Fi does not connect or keeps dropping
problem: The laptop shows 'No internet' or the signal drops.
steps: Turn Wi-Fi off and on, or use Airplane mode on and off.
Check other devices: if they also fail, tell the Service Desk; the office internet may be down.
Open Settings, Network & internet, Wi-Fi, choose the network, and select Forget. Connect again with the Wi-Fi password.
Move closer to the access point. In the garage and charging area the signal is weaker.
Restart the laptop.
still: If one place always drops, send us the room name. We will check the signal strength and may move an access point.
prevent: Do not connect company devices to public Wi-Fi without the VPN.
ticket: Network and VPN, Medium (Urgent if the whole office is affected)
shot: The Wi-Fi settings page with the Forget button.

title: What to do if you clicked a suspicious link or e-mail
problem: You opened an e-mail link or file and you are not sure it was safe, or you typed your password on a strange page.
steps: Do not panic and do not delete anything.
Disconnect the computer from the network (turn Wi-Fi off or unplug the cable).
Call the Service Desk immediately. Say: 'I may have clicked a phishing link.'
Do not keep using the same password anywhere. We will reset your password and check your account.
Forward the e-mail as an attachment to the security mailbox so we can block it for everyone.
still: If a message asks for money or gift cards, tell us even if you did not click.
prevent: Check the sender address, hover over links, and never enter your password after clicking a link in an e-mail.
shot: An example phishing e-mail with the sender address highlighted (use a harmless training sample).

title: How to request new software or a licence
problem: You need a program that is not installed.
steps: Check the approved software list on the intranet. Approved programs can be installed by us in minutes.
Create a ticket in the Software and Licences category with the program name and why you need it.
Your manager approves the request when a licence costs money.
We install the program remotely or ask you to be present. Do not download installers yourself.
still: If the program is not on the list, we check security and cost before we approve it.
prevent: Request software at least two working days before you need it.
ticket: Software and Licences, Medium or Low
shot: The ticket form with the category selected.

title: Sending large files (over 20 MB)
problem: Your message bounces with 'message too large'.
steps: Company mail accepts attachments up to 20 MB in total.
Save the file in the shared folder or cloud drive and right-click it, then choose Copy link.
Paste the link in your e-mail. Check who can open it.
For very large files (video, drawings), ask us for a temporary upload area.
still: If the link says 'access denied', share the folder with the recipient's name.
prevent: Zip large folders and remove unused images before sending.
shot: The Copy link option on a shared file.

title: Multi-factor authentication code does not arrive
applies: Authenticator app on iPhone and Android
problem: You are asked for an MFA code or approval but nothing arrives.
steps: Check that phone notifications are enabled for the Authenticator app.
Open the app by hand; the code may be inside it even if no notification came.
Check the phone has internet and that date and time are automatic.
If you changed phones, you must register the app again; contact the Service Desk.
Never share the code with anyone, even someone who says they are from IT.
still: If you lost your phone, call us immediately so we can protect your account.
prevent: Keep a second sign-in method registered, such as a work phone number.
ticket: Accounts and Access, Medium (High if the phone is lost)

title: Getting access to a shared folder or shared mailbox
applies: Windows file shares and Exchange shared mailboxes
problem: You moved teams or the folder suddenly says 'access denied'.
steps: Check the exact folder path from the e-mail or ticket.
Ask your manager to approve access in the ticket.
We add you to the correct security group. Access normally works after you sign out and sign in.
For a shared mailbox, restart Outlook and wait up to 30 minutes for it to appear.
still: If it still does not appear, send us a screenshot of the error and the path.
prevent: Do not share passwords to open someone else's folder; ask for proper access.
ticket: Accounts and Access, Low (Medium if work is blocked)
shot: The 'Access denied' message with the folder path.

title: Printer shows Offline or does not print
problem: The printer is on, but your document stays in the queue or the printer says Offline.
steps: Check the printer screen for paper jams, empty paper or toner messages.
Open Settings, Bluetooth & devices, Printers & scanners, choose the printer, then Open print queue. Cancel stuck jobs.
Restart the printer and wait two minutes.
Ask a colleague if they can print. If yes, only your computer has the problem.
Remove the printer and add it again by its IP address (ask the Service Desk for the address).
still: If nobody can print, the printer's IP address may have changed; report it as a printer ticket.
prevent: Printers have a fixed IP reserved in the router so the address does not change.
ticket: Printers and Scanners, Low (Medium if the department cannot print at all)
shot: The Printers & scanners settings page and the print queue.

title: Windows Update is stuck or fails
problem: Updates stay at the same percentage for a long time or fail with an error.
steps: Wait at least 30 minutes; some updates are large.
Restart the laptop and try Settings, Windows Update, Check for updates again.
Open Settings, System, Troubleshoot, Other troubleshooters, and run the Windows Update troubleshooter.
Make sure the disk has at least 15 GB free (see KB-06).
If it still fails, tell us the error code shown.
still: We can reset the update cache from the command line (support staff only).
prevent: Leave the laptop plugged in and on during updates.
shot: The Windows Update page; the troubleshooter result.

title: Linux server: names do not resolve (DNS problem)
problem: 'ping 8.8.8.8' works but 'ping google.com' says 'Temporary failure in name resolution'.
steps: Check the connection: 'ip a' and 'ip route'.
Check DNS: 'resolvectl status'. If no DNS server is listed, DNS is the problem.
Edit the netplan file in '/etc/netplan/' and add the nameservers under the interface.
Apply: 'sudo netplan apply'. Test again with 'ping google.com'.
Document the change in the ticket.
still: If DNS servers are listed but the lookup fails, test another server: 'resolvectl query google.com'.
prevent: Keep a copy of the working netplan file before editing.
ticket: Network and VPN (Infrastructure and Network L2)

title: Linux server: disk is almost full
problem: A server says 'No space left on device' or df -h shows over 90%.
steps: Check usage: 'df -h'.
Find the big folders: 'sudo du -sh /var/* | sort -h'.
Look for old logs ('/var/log') and the package cache ('/var/cache/apt').
Run the disk cleanup script in dry-run mode first, then for real.
Verify with 'df -h' and note the freed space in the ticket.
still: If the space is used by an application's data, do not delete it; tell the owner.
prevent: Set up log rotation and monitor disk usage weekly.
shot: The 'df -h' output before and after cleanup.

title: Teams camera, microphone or headset not working
problem: Others cannot see or hear you in a meeting.
steps: Open Teams, Settings, Devices, and choose the correct camera, microphone and speaker.
Check the Windows privacy settings: Settings, Privacy & security, Camera / Microphone, and allow apps.
Unplug and plug the USB headset into another port.
Restart Teams and test again with 'Make a test call'.
If still not working, update the audio/camera driver from Device Manager.
still: If the device does not appear in Device Manager, it may be broken; we will replace it.
prevent: Test your equipment five minutes before important meetings.

title: Charging dashboard is not loading (for dispatchers)
problem: The charging dashboard shows an error or never loads and vehicles cannot be scheduled.
steps: Refresh with Ctrl+F5 and try another browser.
Check other web pages work; if not, see KB-07.
If other pages work, report it immediately as Urgent: vehicles may be waiting to charge.
Give us the time, the page address and a screenshot of the error.
Use the manual charging checklist from the dispatcher binder until we confirm it is fixed.
still: Support staff: check the application service on the server and read its log.
prevent: Report slowness early; a service that restarts at night can fail after backups.
